criteria: Down 20%+ since the flagged earnings report, market cap over $1B, RSI under 30, a real recent earnings miss (or swing to a loss), gross margin still positive and revenue not collapsing (down under 25% YoY, not declining 3+ of the last 4 quarters), excludes banks, pharma, and biotech. Ranked by Reset Score (0 to 100), recomputed daily from live price against the original earnings shock and leadership finding: earnings shock size, price drop severity, a confirmed recent leadership change as a bonus signal, and how well the underlying financial health is actually verified. Cards persist day to day once listed and only drop off once the reset has clearly played out or a genuine new health concern is confirmed, never just for the price falling further.
disclaimer: Informational screener only, not investment advice. Data from live market feed. Not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

cards.name: Nayax
cards.why: Runs a global payments and commerce platform. Swung from an expected profit to an outright loss this quarter, one of the sharpest misses in this group, and shares are down 30% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: StubHub
cards.why: Runs an online marketplace for buying and selling live event tickets. The latest quarter missed estimates by 100%, swinging from an expected profit to breakeven, one of the sharpest misses in this group, with shares down 22% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Vishay Precision Group
cards.why: Makes precision measurement and sensing technology components for industrial and test markets. The latest quarter missed estimates by 79%, one of the sharpest misses in this group, with shares down 25% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Life360
cards.why: Makes a mobile app that helps families track each other's location and stay safe. New CEO Lauren Antonoff took over in August 2025 after founder Chris Hulls stepped back to executive chairman, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 57%, with shares down 33% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Arteris
cards.why: Licenses interconnect technology for semiconductor chip design. New CFO Saurabh Sinha was named in August 2026, succeeding retiring CFO Nick Hawkins, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 67%, with shares down 27% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: BillionToOne
cards.why: Makes molecular diagnostics tests. Missed estimates by 38% this quarter, and shares are down 37% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Knife River
cards.why: Mines aggregates and produces ready-mix concrete, asphalt, and other construction materials. The latest quarter missed estimates by 32%, with shares down 26% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: LeMaitre Vascular
cards.why: Makes medical devices for treating peripheral vascular disease. New CFO Dorian LeBlanc joined in March 2025, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 9%, with shares down 24% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Hut 8 Corp
cards.why: Runs data centers for AI and bitcoin mining. The second quarter swung to a much deeper loss than expected, one of the sharpest misses in this group, with shares down 21% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: ATS Corporation
cards.why: Runs automated manufacturing and assembly systems. New CEO Doug Wright took over in January 2026 after predecessor Andrew Hider's abrupt departure in the middle of 2025, and the first quarter fully under him missed estimates by 14%, a classic leadership reset, with shares down 30% since, while revenue is down modestly, not collapsing. Wright has also bought shares on the open market since taking over.

cards.name: Core Scientific
cards.why: Runs data centers for bitcoin mining and AI computing infrastructure. The second quarter swung to a much deeper loss than expected, one of the sharpest misses in this group, with shares down 21% since, while revenue has kept growing. Director Eric Weiss bought 7,000 shares on the open market in August 2026.

cards.name: Trade Desk
cards.why: Runs a programmatic ad buying platform. Its finance seat has turned over three times in under a year: a CFO out after 6 months, an interim, now a third hire in July, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 8%, with shares down 24% since. CEO Jeff Green has bought roughly $300 million of stock on the open market since March 2026, among the largest insider purchases in the industry.

cards.name: La-Z-Boy
cards.why: Makes and sells residential upholstered furniture through its La-Z-Boy Furniture Galleries stores. The latest quarter missed estimates by 12%, with shares down 22% since, while revenue is down modestly, not collapsing.

cards.name: Dick's Sporting Goods
cards.why: Runs a chain of sporting goods stores that recently absorbed the Foot Locker acquisition. The latest quarter missed estimates by 9%, with shares down 31% since, as the newly acquired Foot Locker business underperformed and the company cut guidance for it. Revenue is up sharply year over year, but that reflects the acquisition, not organic growth. Multiple directors bought a combined $3.7 million of stock on the open market in the days after the report.

cards.name: Tennant Company
cards.why: Makes industrial cleaning equipment for maintaining floors and surfaces in commercial and industrial spaces. The latest quarter missed estimates by 37%, one of the sharper misses in this group, with shares down 23% since, while revenue has held roughly flat. Director Donal Mulligan bought 8,000 shares on the open market in August 2026.

cards.name: Powell Industries
cards.why: Makes custom engineered electrical power distribution equipment. The latest quarter missed estimates by 3%, with shares down 22% since, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: Trinity Industries
cards.why: Runs railcar leasing and manufacturing for the North American rail industry. The latest quarter missed estimates by 7%, with shares down 24% since, while revenue is down modestly, not collapsing.
